_comment: Which permission prompts Imperatorium answers for you.
Deny always wins; anything not matched by a rule is asked about as usual.
Set enabled=false to turn the whole thing off without touching hooks.
never_auto_approve. The most specific matching project path wins.
_decision_format: `object` is the reply Claude Code actually acts on, so verdicts here take effect. Remove the key (legacy reply) to make every verdict advisory again - logged, never applied.

park._comment: Offer an `ask` to the Imperatorium window and Stream Deck before the terminal prompts. While a request waits, the terminal's own prompt is held back, so an interactive session (you may be at its terminal) waits only wait_seconds; a background session has no terminal and waits background_wait_seconds. Nobody answering falls straight through to the normal prompt. Set enabled=false to go back to terminal-only, then rerun hooks/install.py so the hook timeout shrinks too.

_projects: Per-project overrides keyed by absolute path, e.g. {"C:\code\my-app": {"auto_edit": true, "safe_bash": ["make\s+test\b"]}}
_enabled: Auto-approval: true lets this policy answer cheap prompts (reads, git status, tests) for you. false asks about everything, but the window and Stream Deck can still answer prompts. setup_machine.py asks which you want.
